title: Operator timeline and customer review checklist: incident evidence package
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact operator-facing timeline and a customer-ready evidence checklist we can attach to status updates and the customer postmortem. The goal is to give customers: (1) a short, verifiable timeline of what happened; (2) an evidence bundle they can validate; (3) clear options for replay, rollforward, or safe-mode enrollment; and (4) next steps and contacts. Draft language here is intentionally plain so it can be embedded in status page updates and email templates without heavy editing.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
On 2027-02-18 at ~11:03 UTC Redwood ingestion routing entered a transient degraded state affecting a subset of tenant requests to the EU region for approximately 42 minutes. Symptoms: elevated request queueing, partial KV-cache misses, and an increased rate of 5xx responses for model endpoints pinned to rwd-7b-v2. Immediate mitigations restored service routing by 11:45 UTC; full validation and customer-facing replay/verification options are below. We acknowledge impact for affected tenants and offer a guided evidence package and replay choices.

Concise customer-facing timeline (for status page snippets):
- 11:00 UTC — Routine autoscaler reconfiguration triggered rollout of routing policy 7c (internal).
- 11:03 UTC — Traffic shift started; routing controller reported elevated queue depths for EU availability zone AZ-eu-2.
- 11:07 UTC — First tenant-facing 5xxs observed (API error rate to affected tenants > 1.2% threshold).
- 11:12 UTC — Operators enacted automatic fallback to soft-routing pool; partial drop in effective throughput but queueing remained elevated.
- 11:30 UTC — Engineering identified a bug in the routing rollout that disabled a rate-limit shim under heavy batching.
- 11:35 UTC — Hotfix (rollforward) applied to restore rate-limit shim; traffic rebalanced slowly.
- 11:45 UTC — Queue depth and error rates back to normal; monitoring shows recovery.
- 12:05 UTC — Post-recovery validation completed; no data loss detected.

What we observed (technical summary for customers who want more detail):
- Root contributor: a config rollout combined with a batching schedule edge case caused the routing controller to bypass an internal rate-limit guard when continuous batching aggregated large inflight request groups. The guard is intended to prevent burst head-of-line blocking for tenants with high concurrency.
- Mechanism: during the rollout, one controller replica applied the new policy before the cache prime completed; the replica accepted traffic but did not enforce the expected request-shed behavior under high batch sizes, which allowed queues to grow and KV-cache miss amplification to occur.
- Scope: only tenants routed through EU AZ-eu-2 with model variant rwd-7b-v2 and batched traffic pattern > 64 concurrent in-flight tokens experienced increased latency and intermittent 5xx errors. Other regions and model variants were not affected.

Evidence bundle for tenant verification (what we will attach to the status update):
- Operator Timeline CSV: per-second metrics for queue_depth, inflight_batches, 5xx_count, region, AZ, model_variant (CSV file)
- Sample request traces: 10 anonymized trace IDs (redacted tenant identifiers) showing span-level timeline and error codes
- Replay manifest: list of request IDs (redacted) and timestamp ranges available for tenant-initiated replay
- Rate-limit guard config diff: the exact config diff applied during the rollout and the hotfix patch
- Hotfix PR: link to the GitHub PR that contained the fix
- Validation summary: results of post-recovery validation checks (latency percentiles, error rate, cache hit rate)

How customers can validate the evidence (step-by-step):
1) Review the Operator Timeline CSV against your tenant timestamps. Look at queue_depth and 5xx_count columns for correlation to request latencies you observed.
2) Request access to the anonymized trace IDs (we provide the traces in the evidence bundle). Use your internal correlation keys to match events.
3) If you rely on persistent KV state, check the replay manifest and ask us to perform a scoped replay for the listed time range. We can either provide the replay package for you to run in your environment or perform a managed replay with your consent.

Replay and remediation options for tenants (choices we present):
- Managed replay (redwood-run): Redwood runs tenant-scoped replay for the provided timestamp window and returns a verdict of response divergence and an evidence report. This is offered at no cost for impacted tenants in the affected rollout.
- Replay-by-customer: We provide a replay manifest and the request payloads for customers that prefer to run replays internally.
- Rollforward/patch: If a tenant requires a model-pin rollback to rwd-7b-v1 because rwd-7b-v2 latency is unsuitable while we strengthen rollout guards, we can schedule a targeted rollback during a low-traffic window.
- Safe-mode enrollment: Tenants can opt into 'safe-mode'—a routing policy that enforces conservative batching and strict per-tenant rate caps while we harden rollout logic. Enrollment is reversible.

Customer impact and entitlements: 
- Affected tenants will be eligible for a proof-based mitigation (managed replay or credits) per our SLA terms. Specific credit calculation and remedy pathway will be handled by your Customer Success rep.

Immediate actions we took (operator notes):
- Auto-fallback engaged at 11:12 UTC (reduced throughput but limited error blast radius).
- Hotfix deployed 11:35 UTC (PR linked above).
- Scoped validation run 11:45–12:05 UTC; no persistent storage writes were rolled back and no customer data was deleted.
- Post-incident change: rollout orchestration now requires config priming and a rollout health gate that verifies that the rate-limit shim is present on all replicas before applying new routing policies.

Planned follow-ups and timeline:
- 48 hours: publish formal postmortem (technical root cause analysis and long-term mitigations) and distribute an unredacted evidence package to enterprise contacts under NDA.
- 7 days: complete rollout-orchestration hardening and additional unit/integration tests for the shim gating logic.
- 30 days: publish a customer-facing engineering review that details code and config changes with annotated diffs.

Suggested customer-facing phrasing for status page update (short snippet):
"We experienced a routing configuration issue in EU on 2027-02-18 that affected a subset of tenants for ~42 minutes. We deployed a fix and validated recovery. We are providing an evidence bundle and replay options to impacted customers—see attached checklist for steps and options. Your Customer Success rep will reach out with next steps."

Operator checklist before attaching evidence to a status update (do not publish until these are satisfied):
- [ ] Sanitize tenant identifiers in traces and CSV (confirm redaction policy applied)
- [ ] Include at least 3 trace examples demonstrating failure and 3 demonstrating successful post-fix responses
- [ ] Confirm hotfix PR is merged and deployed across EU replicas
- [ ] Generate replay manifest and verify checksums of attached payloads
- [ ] Confirm legal/Privacy review for any evidence sharing with enterprise tenants (if unredacted)
notes: Draft intended for quick adaptation into status page copy or customer emails. Replace placeholders with tenant-specific contact info and attach the CSV and trace bundle. Use the linked Confluence doc for full operator runbook and the GitHub PR for the technical patch.
